Marine microalgal growth inhibition data with censored cell counts

Source: R/data.R
alga.Rd

Final cell density and average specific growth rate for two marine microalgae exposed to each of two contaminants, consolidated from four growth inhibition tests. The species are the symbiotic dinoflagellate Cladocopium proliferum ("c_proliferum") and the cryptophyte Rhodomonas salina ("r_salina"). Each test ran a dilution series against an unexposed control with five replicate cultures per exposure level, and twice that at the control.

Format

An object of class data.frame with 310 rows and 9 columns.

Details

This dataset exists to demonstrate two data-preparation problems that arise before any model is fitted: what a response owes to the control mean it is referenced against, and what to do with counts that fell below the resolution the method could record.

Cell density is counted to a resolution of 10. A recorded density of 0 therefore means "fewer than 10 cells", not "no cells". The growth rate such a culture implies is bounded rather than undefined, and left-censoring at the growth rate implied by a density of 10 is the treatment the recording process actually justifies.

Growth rate is reported exactly as supplied, including substituted values, with sgr_source marking them. Where density was recorded as 0 the source set the growth rate to 0. That substitution repays a look: a growth rate of 0 means "no change", and it sits in the middle of the observed range — above every genuinely negative value in the same test — so a culture that was lost entirely is recorded as less affected than one that was merely declining. Correcting it in the shipped data would remove the example, and substitution at a boundary is the practice vignette("example6") argues against.

The two species grow on very different scales, which is why they were run over different exposure durations — seven days for C. proliferum against three for R. salina. Symbiodiniaceae divide slowly, and control cultures multiplied only about 2–3 fold over the whole exposure, against about 17–73 fold for R. salina; control growth rates differ by roughly an order of magnitude between them. Only R. salina was driven below the counting resolution, in 16 of its 85 cultures under contaminant A and 4 of its 70 under contaminant B; C. proliferum never was.

The contrast is useful in itself: a slow grower gives a small dynamic range between control and complete inhibition, so the same absolute error in a count is a much larger error in growth rate.

Wherever a density was measured, the growth rate satisfies sgr = (log(density) - log(density_initial)) / days. That holds exactly for contaminant A, and to the three decimals the source rounded to for contaminant B — itself a milder instance of the same recording problem. density_initial and days are supplied so that growth rates can be recomputed and the censoring bound derived.

The contaminants are anonymised and the exposure units are not stated. Dose values are the tested nominal concentrations on an undisclosed scale, so their relative spacing — and therefore every toxicity estimate derived from them — is preserved. The two contaminants are on different undisclosed scales and their dose values are not comparable with each other.

The columns are as follows:

species

Test species (fct), "c_proliferum" (Cladocopium proliferum) or "r_salina" (Rhodomonas salina).

contaminant

The contaminant, anonymised as A or B (fct).

dose

Nominal exposure concentration, undisclosed units; 14 levels including the control for contaminant A, 13 for contaminant B (dbl).

dose_measured

Measured exposure concentration, undisclosed units. Recorded for contaminant B only; NA throughout contaminant A (dbl).

density

Final cell density, counted to a resolution of 10. A 0 means the count fell below that resolution (int).

sgr

Average specific growth rate per day, exactly as supplied. A substituted 0 wherever density is 0 (dbl).

sgr_source

How sgr arose (fct), either "measured" or "substituted".

days

Exposure duration in days (int).

density_initial

Cell density at the start of the exposure (dbl).

Examples

head(alga)
#>        species contaminant dose dose_measured density       sgr sgr_source days
#> 1 c_proliferum           A    0            NA   18590 0.1210272   measured    7
#> 2 c_proliferum           A    0            NA   17720 0.1141801   measured    7
#> 3 c_proliferum           A    0            NA   17490 0.1123137   measured    7
#> 4 c_proliferum           A    0            NA   17110 0.1091757   measured    7
#> 5 c_proliferum           A    0            NA   19740 0.1296019   measured    7
#> 6 c_proliferum           A    0            NA   19200 0.1256395   measured    7
#>   density_initial
#> 1            7968
#> 2            7968
#> 3            7968
#> 4            7968
#> 5            7968
#> 6            7968
with(alga, table(species, contaminant, sgr_source))
#> , , sgr_source = measured
#> 
#>               contaminant
#> species         A  B
#>   c_proliferum 85 70
#>   r_salina     69 66
#> 
#> , , sgr_source = substituted
#> 
#>               contaminant
#> species         A  B
#>   c_proliferum  0  0
#>   r_salina     16  4
#>
